Hi Alex — great to hear procurement is ready to move. I pulled together an initial MAP and a short checklist (attached). High level answers inline, and I’ve looped in Karthik for the marketplace/private-offer specifics and Marissa for capacity / billing ops.

Quick answers:
- MPO vs vendor invoice: MPO (AWS Private Offer) is the cleanest for Cirrus if you want charges to appear on the AWS invoice; we can also accept a vendor invoice to invoices@cirrushealth.com if your finance needs a vendor relationship. Either works but MPO requires acceptance steps on the AWS side.
- SOC2 & security: we’ll attach SOC2 Type II report and an IP/data flow diagram. I can share SSO onboarding notes if needed.
- Timeline: assuming MPO acceptance, expected close is ~10 business days once procurement confirms PO content; vendor invoice path can be faster if you already have procurement wiring.

I’ve attached Redwood-PO-Checklist.pdf — it lists the docs procurement typically asks for and the minimum PO language we require. Karthik — can you confirm MPO steps and term sheet we should send to their procurement team? Marissa — can we provide an estimate for initial reserved capacity (they asked about latency-critical workloads)?

Next step: Alex, can you share the contact who will actually click Accept on the AWS MPO? If you can copy them on the next note we’ll include acceptance steps.

Alex / Monica — quick technical/procurement note from the Marketplace ops side. Attaching our standard term sheet for Private Offers. Key steps and estimated lead times: 

1) Term sheet & PO content (1–2 business days): we send MPO term sheet (attached). Procurement confirms PO line items and billing party.
2) AWS creates the offer; Redwood approves & submits to you (1 business day).
3) Cirrus accepts the MPO in the AWS Marketplace console (owner action) — acceptance is required to bind billing to AWS account (same-day if the acceptor has console access).
4) AWS billing propagation (1–3 business days): once accepted, charges flow via AWS invoice; AWS may take an invoice cycle to reflect subscriptions. If you need immediate vendor invoicing, Redwood will issue the first invoice on signature instead.
5) Final enablement & onboarding (2–5 business days): we schedule a short enablement call and provision reserved capacity if included.

Risks / notes: if the PO involves custom tax or specific invoice terms, it can add a week for legal review. For a firm end-of-October close we recommend starting acceptance no later than Oct 23.

Attached: AWS-PrivateOffer-TermSheet.pdf. Marissa — can you follow up with an estimate for 8–16 vGPU capacity and a proposed start date?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
